title: Token monitoring & lightweight skills
intro: Context is rent. I measure the initial instruction/catalog tax and the tool results added during work: on-demand skills, requestable rules, bounded outputs, and a brutal always-on budget.
why: Every always-on rule, tool schema, fat skill description, and unbounded command result competes with the actual job. Cutting that tax isn’t stinginess — it’s how the working relationship stays fast and legible.

practices.title: Thin skill dispatchers
practices.body: SKILL.md stays short; deep detail lives in reference.md loaded only when needed.

practices.title: Requestable by default
practices.body: Most rules are pull-when-relevant. Always-on is reserved for true P0 fail-closed constraints.

practices.title: Lean MCP sessions
practices.body: Tiny always-on core (memory + decisions + app control). Enable specialty servers for the task, then unload.

practices.title: Measure the tax
practices.body: Measure both the stable prefix and what tools inject later. One Hansei found 17 oversized results contributing 95% of a 2.26 MB task payload.

practices.title: Encode the second burn
practices.body: If a failure repeats, write a thin skill — do not keep re-explaining in a growing chat.

practices.title: Split lanes, not prompts
practices.body: Parallel tasks with clear owns beat one mega-context trying to do everything — if review and coordination cost less than the split saves.

practices.title: Bound before context
practices.body: Filter logs, cap command output, and pass images at the detail actually needed. Tool-result hygiene starts before the call, not after a huge result arrives.

practices.title: One bounded diagnostic pass
practices.body: When a human explicitly asks for a check, batch the minimum evidence, answer from it, and stop. A second pass needs a real unresolved blocker.

practices.title: Keep three ledgers separate
practices.body: Current quota-window use, cumulative task tokens, and cached-input volume answer different questions. A rollover or cache hit does not erase the work.

practices.title: Reviews do not clean up
practices.body: Measurement is read-only. Report optional tools or excess context; do not unload, archive, rewrite, or otherwise mutate them unless cleanup was separately requested.

antiPatterns: Always-on essays that restate the whole philosophy every turn
Leaving optional MCPs loaded “just in case”
Past chats as the only memory (prompt archaeology)
Counting LOC or tokens-spent as success
Using another agent as a watcher, timer, or polling sensor
Running repeated quick checks after the human said to stop automated checks
Treating cached input as free or a quota reset as task-level accounting
Hiding cleanup flags inside a read-only audit
